evals.prompt: design this new service to handle 10x traffic growth
evals.expected_output: Externalizes session/cache state out of the app tier so any instance can serve any request, chooses horizontal vs vertical scaling per component deliberately (e.g. horizontal app tier, vertical-then-partition for a single-writer database), and identifies which component would saturate first at 10x load.

evals.prompt: we keep adding app server instances but throughput stopped improving
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses that a shared bottleneck downstream of the stateless tier (a single-writer database, shared lock, or serialized queue) is capping capacity regardless of app instance count, and recommends confirming it empirically via profiling/load-testing then partitioning or offloading it rather than adding more app boxes.

evals.prompt: sessions keep breaking on other instances, let's just add sticky sessions to fix it
evals.expected_output: Pushes back that sticky routing papers over statefulness instead of removing it and reintroduces a single point of failure per session; recommends externalizing session state to a shared cache or database so any instance can serve any request.
